summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Located UN WPP 2024 data, dataset documentation and methodology report as the single source for destination ageing indicators, plus OECD IMO 2025 (health/care workforce migration) and Japan's acceptance framework as demand-side policy evidence. All demographic values are pending. Key methodological issue: WPP totals for GCC states include non-national migrants, so working-age projections there reflect migration assumptions rather than native ageing; native vs non-native split must come from GLMM/national sources.

findings.claim: Q1: Projected old-age dependency ratio and working-age population change 2025-2050 for each major destination (GCC six, Malaysia, Japan, Korea, Australia, UK, Canada, India).
findings.note: Required: WPP 2024 medium variant, population by age for listed countries, 2025, 2030, 2040, 2050 (plus low/high variants).

findings.claim: Q1: Native (national) working-age trajectory for GCC states separated from migrant stock.
findings.note: Required: GLMM national/non-national population by age; WPP net-migration assumption per GCC state (methodology report).

findings.claim: Q1: Translation of ageing into foreign-labour demand by sector (care, construction, manufacturing, agriculture).
findings.note: Required: destination labour-demand projections or policy caps (Japan SSW caps, Korea EPS quotas, OECD health-workforce chapter). No elasticity is assumed without evidence.

findings.claim: Ageing raises structural demand for foreign labour mainly in high-income East Asian and European destinations; for GCC states demand is driven by economic diversification and localisation policy rather than native ageing. This is a working hypothesis to be tested against WPP and policy data, not a finding.
WPP 2024 medium variant is the reference; low and high variants are reported as the uncertainty band.

data_gaps: No official destination-level projections of foreign-labour demand by sector were located (only policy caps).
GCC native/non-native age structures are published irregularly and with mixed vintages.
A WPP revision after 2024 (if released) not verified; confirm latest vintage on retrieval.

assumptions.text: Destination list follows 23A DoFE destinations plus India and main education destinations; revised once 23A concentration values are retrieved.

challenges.text: Nepal's own WPP projections imply a closing demographic window; outward labour supply parameters should be linked to Nepal's working-age projection rather than held constant.
Scenarios assuming sustained GCC demand should test localisation (23B PC-01) against the ageing-driven East Asian demand shift.

uncertainty: High. No projections retrieved. WPP migration assumptions dominate GCC projections, and the link from ageing to foreign-labour demand is policy-mediated and not directly measurable from demographic data.
